notes: In verify.report(), a page counts as complete only when its page_completion reading_keys exactly equal sorted(set(fragments[scan])) (verify.py:85). Fragment keys come from four places: unit segment fragments (stem/lang), citations (citation/<stem>/<lang>/<i>, keyed by citation['scan'], verify.py:34-36), documentary instructions that have a scan (instruction/<name>, verify.py:44-47), and front pages and review_payloads. Navigation keys are only added to `pending`. They never go into `fragments` (verify.py:39-43).

s320, s323 and s326: the only difference between recorded and current is one added citation key on each page: citation/musaf_shir_shel_yom/he/0, citation/rh_minchah_ashrei/he/0 and citation/rh_minchah_haazinu_levi/he/0. These match verify.py:34-36. Each has an existing review record with complete=true, source_review_complete=true, no unresolved items, and source_scans that include that page. The proposal therefore adds no new source acceptance. It brings three citations that were already reviewed into the page ledger.

s325: the only difference is that navigation/rh_minchah_returns/he is removed. The verifier never puts navigation keys in fragments, so the recorded list can never match, and removing the key is correct. Navigation review still counts. Its review_is_current check feeds `pending`, and `complete` requires `not pending` (verify.py:93). An existing complete review record for that key also lists s325 among its source_scans.
All four current lists are already sorted and have no duplicates, so they meet the sorted(set(...)) comparison.

No unit, segment or instruction key is added or dropped on any page apart from the citation and navigation changes above. This is consistent with source_words_changed=false and an empty pending_review_payloads.
